critical_code_review_comments: sandbox_runner.py: asyncio.to_thread refactor is clean and correct — worker-thread isolation for the e2b sync client is the right fix. Consider adding a per-call timeout on `asyncio.wait_for()` around `asyncio.to_thread(...)` — right now if e2b hangs beyond `timeout=15`, the worker thread stays alive indefinitely (thread leak) even though the async call resolves via the exception path only on ImportError. Not blocking, but a slow-drift risk if e2b starts hanging.

db_restore.restore_to_scratch: prefix-scoped drop is safe, but if the DB already has a legitimate user collection whose name starts with `_restore_scratch_` (extremely unlikely, but no invariant enforces this), it would be dropped by _drop_prefixed. Consider adding a length/timestamp regex check on the prefix before dropping. Very low risk.

rca_of_the_issue: Fixes validated. Root cause of prior deploy flapping: (1) e2b_code_interpreter.Sandbox is a SYNC client that was being invoked directly from `async def` handlers, blocking the entire uvicorn event loop for 1-2s per sandbox call — starving the /api/health handler and causing nginx upstream timeouts / K8s probe flaps. Fix: wrap sync work in asyncio.to_thread(). (2) restore_to_scratch tried to create a second Mongo database (aurem_scratch_restore_*), which Atlas app-scoped users cannot do → OperationFailure code 13 on every drill run. Fix: restore into prefixed collections in DB_NAME. Both fixes verified in isolation and end-to-end here.
